description: The pie chart represents the distribution of difficulty across data entries, comparing five categories. There are five slices in total, labeled as "Very easy", "Very hard", "Easy", "Hard", and "Medium". The "Medium" slice, colored red, accounts for approximately 51.8% of the chart. The "Hard" slice, colored blue, represents around 25.7%. The "Easy" slice, colored green, makes up about 11.2%, while the "Very hard" slice, colored orange, constitutes roughly 6.5%. Lastly, the "Very easy" slice, colored purple, comprises approximately 4.7%. The chart includes a legend that maps colors to labels and displays percentage labels outside the slices for the "Medium", "Very easy", "Very hard", and "Easy" categories. The slices are arranged in a clockwise order, starting with "Medium" and followed by "Hard", "Easy", "Very hard", and "Very easy", with no slices visually emphasized.
